task.title: Atomically materialize the next due schedule
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/847 by binding deterministic pending-schedule selection and caller-identified task creation in one atomic kernel operation.
acceptance_criteria: Select the earliest pending due schedule by due instant then exact schedule ID and materialize it as the caller-owned task.
Return none when no work is due, preserve schedules on task identity collision, and restart only after persisted schedule conflicts.
Accept direct pending materialization in fail-closed replay and preserve exact history and task provenance without clock, dispatch, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: Schedule-store acceptance tests failed because materialize_next_due did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused tests for deterministic selection, no due work, task collision, reopen and provenance, competing transitions, and malformed discovered history.

attempts.summary: Implemented the atomic kernel boundary and reconciled lifecycle replay.
attempts.diagnostic: The existing claim-next and exact claimed-materialization operations left an avoidable process-failure gap for callers that already owned a task identity.
attempts.patch: Selected the exact pending revision, atomically appended schedule.materialized and task.started, retried only persisted schedule conflicts, and accepted both direct pending and explicit claimed materialization histories.

attempts.summary: Clarified the exact persistence contract after substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit identified ambiguous documentation about whether task.started was new and what complete projection success returned; incremental review of the correction was temporarily rate limited.
attempts.patch: Aligned ADR and scheduler wording around ExpectedVersion::NoStream, updated revision and task binding, kept auto-merge disabled through the cooldown, and required genuine exact-head review before merge.

outcome.summary: Callers that already own a cutoff and task identity can atomically consume the deterministic next due intent without a recoverable claim gap or execution authority.

lessons: When identity is already caller-owned, one atomic schedule/task append avoids inventing claim-recovery policy.
The review found ambiguous documentation about whether task.started was new and what complete projection success returned; the ADR and scheduler wording were aligned before merge.
Replay must explicitly validate every newly legal transition while retaining fail-closed corruption behavior.
A rate-limited incremental review is false green; preserve the PR until the exact head receives substantive review.
